summary: Replace the random search with a deterministic construction: integer-embedded simplex sets {x in N^d : sum x_i ≤ n}, where the sumset and difference set sizes are known in closed form. The code picks the best (d, n) pair with at most 4000 points, using base 2n+1 so sums and differences stay distinct

Generalise the simplex construction to a truncated simplex {x in N^d : sum x ≤ n, each x_i ≤ m}, which gives more freedom in the (d, n, m) choice. Generalise the simplex to weighted simplices {x ∈ N^d : Σ w_i x_i ≤ n} with weights in {1,2,3}. This gives much finer control over set size near the 4000 limit and different shapes. Candidates are evaluated exactly with numpy under a time budget, and the closed-form simplex is kept as the fallback.

Start from the best closed-form simplex and run a time-limited local search on it. The search adds or removes points (shell points just outside the simplex, boundary points inside it), tracking exact sum and difference multiplicities in dicts, and keeps a move only if log|A-A|/log|A+A| improves. The existing search stops at d<12, but the size limit of 4000 and the magnitude bound allow dimensions up to about 15 with n=4. I extended the d range to 40 and replaced the loose base bound with the actual maximum element, n·B^(d-1) ≤ 1e15.

Keep the simplex family but also scan the integer embedding base B below 2n+1 for the top closed-form candidates. Carries then merge more sums than differences, which may raise the ratio, and each candidate is evaluated exactly with chunked numpy under a time budget, with the baseline as fallback.

Keep the exact base scan but cap it at about 40 s. Then hill-climb on per-coordinate integer weights (the embedding becomes x·w instead of x·B^i) for the best simplex found. Mild collisions that merge sums and differences by similar amounts should raise log|A-A|/log|A+A|, so moves are accepted only

Keeps the simplex scan and weight hill-climb with shorter deadlines, then adds simulated annealing over small integer sets (size 6 to 60) maximising log|A-A|/log|A+A|. The best small set is raised to a Cartesian power embedded in base 2·max+1, which keeps the ratio and grows the size to about 4000.
